definition: In this historical source, psychologism means a philosophical method that begins with the subject, especially by examining consciousness or the process of knowing, rather than starting from objective reality. It is presented as the approach Gioberti opposed when he contrasted a psychological method with an ontological one.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Ontologism; pinned source text

reasons: The provided packet does not define the term “psychologism.” It only references “(see PSYCHOLOGISM)” within an “Ontologism” entry, without supplying a corresponding definition for psychologism.

The definition claims specific meaning (“begins with the subject… examining consciousness or the process of knowing…”) and a specific contrast (Gioberti opposed it vs an ontological method), but the packet only states that Gioberti said modern philosophy “proceeded from an examination… of consciousness or the process of knowing” and that Descartes substituted a “psychologic method”—it does not explicitly identify what “psychologism” means in those terms.

The definition relies on historical interpretation (“In this historical source… presented as the approach Gioberti opposed…”) that is not directly supported as a standalone definition of “psychologism” in the packet.
